summary: Screening for a North Dakota household of one (no children, owns home). Not enough reliable information to recommend any programme. Child-based programmes (TANF, WIC, CHIP, CTC, school meals) do not apply with no children and no pregnancy reported. Earnings from work could not be established after several tries; the answers were inconsistent. Savings/investments were reported at roughly $900,000 to $1.2 million, which rules out SSI and likely rules out asset-tested programmes. Other income was reported at roughly $2,500 to $3,500 a year. Age 65+ and disability status are unclear. Earnings, age 65+ and disability status decide whether Medicaid, SNAP, EITC or ACA premium tax credit could apply, so a caseworker should confirm these before any application.
